answer: Starting from trusted anchors such as jade, zenith, and hollow, let trust propagate along bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph. An adversarial set S with low conductance, Φ(S)=cut(S,S̄)/vol(S), has a sparse external cut, limiting walk flow into it. With capped attestations and seed-based initialization, min-cut transitivity bounds the trust mass, and thus aggregate voting weight, reachable within S; internal Sybil links cannot create trust by themselves.
